Test method and limits
The tests rasterize generated codes, alter their pixels, then run the same reader used here. They do not extract payloads from SVG metadata. Each cell reports successful reads out of the tested messages.
Cover percentages refer to a square mask within the data area. Damage position matters: recovery requires enough surviving shape information and codewords in every block. Losing a corner motif can prevent camera alignment even when enough data survives.
This is synthetic testing, not physical camera or printer validation. The camera reader takes three short snapshots, tries the sharpest first, and locates each frame independently. It tracks the last detected region to focus sharpness scoring. It does not blend moving frames. Glare, curved surfaces, focus and real screen interference still need physical trials.

        
RS Code format and QR feature coverage
Implemented: UTF-8 text and arbitrary bytes, four sizes, four Reed–Solomon protection levels, erasure recovery, byte interleaving, checksums, format identification, themed landmark detection, projective alignment, rotation/reflection attempts, inverted colours, partial-image recovery when alignment succeeds, and structured append up to 16 parts.
RS Code is not ISO QR Code and does not scan in ordinary QR readers. QR-specific numeric/alphanumeric/Kanji compression, ECI and GS1/FNC1 modes are not implemented. UTF-8 and binary carry the content without those specialised compression conventions. Extreme perspective, curved surfaces and arbitrary missing regions remain outside the tested operating range.
